skill.name: architecture-navigator
skill.description: Navigate the DevPrep AI seven-folder frontend architecture, scan local structure, and recommend exact placement paths for features, shared code, integrations, state, types, styles, and routes.
skill.summary: Navigate DevPrep AI architecture and choose the right folder for code changes.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and architecture documentation text. The included shell scanner performs read-only local project inspection, and I found no command injection, network access, exfiltration, destructive behavior, or prompt injection.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running scripts/scan_architecture.sh and document that it reads local file names and counts.
Label command snippets as optional read-only checks and avoid suggesting automatic execution in sensitive workspaces.

static_findings.snippet: 6. **Types Are Global**: Put shared types in types/ to avoid circular dependencies
1. **Is it a route/page?** → `app/` (but keep minimal, import from modules/)
| "Where should social login go?" | `modules/auth/` - Feature-specific authentication logic |
| "Where should I add payment processing?" | `modules/payments/` - New feature module for payment do
| "Where do reusable buttons go?" | `shared/components/ui/Button.tsx` - Reusable UI component |
| "Where's the Claude AI integration?" | `lib/claude/` - External service integration |
| "Where should shopping cart state go?" | `store/cartStore.ts` - Global state management |
| "Where do API types go?" | `types/ai/api.ts` - Shared TypeScript definitions |
- ✅ Shared components are in `shared/`, not duplicated
1. Run `scripts/scan_architecture.sh` to generate current architecture map
The OAuth client setup (SDK wrapper) should go in `lib/oauth/client.ts` (external integration).
**Manual invocation:** Use `/architecture` or explicitly request "scan the architecture".
4. **Reference rules**: Point to `architecture-rules.md` for detailed justification
2. **Notification State** → `store/uiStore.ts` (global state for managing active toasts)

content.value_statement: Large feature work can drift across folders and create unclear dependencies. This skill maps the DevPrep AI architecture and recommends exact placement paths.
actual_capabilities: Scan a DevPrep AI project for the seven-folder architecture.
List feature modules, shared components, API locations, and quick file counts.
Recommend folders for features, routes, shared UI, integrations, state, types, and styles.
Validate placement choices against documented import rules and forbidden patterns.
Explain architecture decisions with concise path-specific reasoning.
limitations: Designed for the DevPrep AI frontend layout, not arbitrary repository structures.
The scanner reads local file names and counts but does not analyze full code semantics.
Architecture guidance depends on the project following the documented seven-folder model.
It can suggest structure but does not automatically refactor code.

use_cases.title: Place a New Feature
use_cases.description: Find the right module, shared folder, state file, type location, or integration path before building.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Drift
use_cases.description: Compare planned changes with import rules and catch misplaced business logic or cross-module dependencies.

use_cases.title: Onboard to the Codebase
use_cases.description: Summarize existing folders, modules, and key locations so new contributors understand the project layout.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Where should I add [feature or component] in DevPrep AI? Explain the path and rule.

prompt_templates.title: Scan the Current Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the architecture and summarize existing modules, shared components, API locations, and quick stats.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Proposed Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned file layout for [feature]. Identify misplaced files and propose corrected paths.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Feature Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the folder structure for [complex feature]. Include module files, shared assets, state, types, and import direction checks.

output_examples.output: The feature behavior belongs in modules/auth. The provider wrapper belongs in lib/oauth because it is an external integration.

output_examples.input: What modules exist in this project?
output_examples.output: A concise architecture map lists current modules, key shared locations, API areas, and quick file counts.
The toast component should be shared, global notification state should live in store, and feature modules should consume the shared hook.

best_practices: Run the architecture scan before answering placement questions in an unfamiliar checkout.
Give exact paths and name the architecture rule behind each recommendation.
Check import direction rules before approving cross-folder dependencies.
anti_patterns: Putting business logic directly in app route files.
Creating cross-module imports between feature folders.
Moving utilities into shared before a second real use exists.

faq.question: What architecture does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the DevPrep AI seven-folder frontend architecture.

faq.question: Does it change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides scanning guidance and placement recommendations; users still approve edits.

faq.question: Can it inspect existing modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run local listing commands or the included scanner to summarize current modules.

faq.question: Does it use network access?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the reviewed files. The scanner uses local shell commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Describe the feature, its users, whether it is shared, and any state or integration needs.
